developments.text: Washington proposed 15% with a possible rise to 20%; Tokyo protested but the rate is in line with the 2025 trade deal.
developments.title: US 15% tariff on Japan

developments.text: The summary of the BoJ's October meeting suggested many board members see a near-term hike as necessary, and Governor Ueda signalled a December move is possible.
developments.title: BoJ December hike watch

for_malaysia: Currency channel: a yen near 159 per dollar makes Japanese goods cheaper relative to Malaysian exports; a BoJ hike in December would ease that. Japan is also a major investor in Malaysian manufacturing, so a tariff deal that holds near 15% limits the knock-on effect.
gaps: JGB 10Y yield not confirmed for this session.
BoJ policy rate level not confirmed from an allowed source this run.
headline: The Nikkei won back under a third of Wednesday's 2.8% drop, and Tokyo protested a proposed 15% US tariff.
numbers_note: Nothing passed the filter on Thursday; the story was Wednesday's 2.78% Nikkei drop, and the yen staying near 159 matters more than any one day's move.

points.text: The Nikkei 225 rose 0.86% to 57,499.16 and the Topix rose just 0.11% to 3,750.4, a day after the Nikkei fell 2.78% to 57,011.62 in the AI sell-off.

The US plans a 15% levy on Japanese imports over alleged excess capacity, which could rise to 20%; Chief Cabinet Secretary Minoru Kihara said Japan has no structural excess capacity and has told Washington it regrets the move.
The yen was around 159.06 per dollar in Asian trading on Thursday, up 0.1%.
The gap between the Nikkei's 0.86% gain and the Topix's 0.11% means a handful of chip and AI heavyweights did the lifting; the broad market barely moved.
